sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup, profile and server start
sections.what: Explains the speed test and its simulated phone profile, reads the page paths, and starts the production server unless a base address is given. It also starts the browser.
sections.why: The header states the profile and budgets so readers can see what is measured.
sections.watch_out: The browser path is used only when it exists, so on another computer a different browser may give different timings.

sections.name: results
sections.title: Measurement loop and report
sections.what: For each path, loads the page several times with the phone profile and cache off, takes the median content timing, adds up script size, and prints the report. It exits with an error if any budget is missed.
sections.why: Likely reason: the median reduces the effect of one unusually fast or slow load.
sections.watch_out: If the content timing never fires, the value is recorded as zero, which passes the speed budget falsely. A page that does not return status 200 also fails the speed budget.

summary: Measures how fast a page's main content appears and how large its script files are, on a simulated slow phone, against the performance budgets.
purpose: Checks that the app meets its speed budgets before a release.
why: The budgets are written in the frontend guide, and this script measures them the same way each time.
how: Optionally starts the production app server, then for each path loads the page several times with a slow-network and slow-CPU profile and the cache turned off. It records the content timing and total script size, takes the median timing, prints JSON, and exits with an error if a budget is missed.
inputs: One or more page paths on the command line, the base address (default local port 3300), and a run count setting that defaults to 3.
outputs: A JSON report with the profile, the timings per run, the median, script size in kilobytes, and an ok flag for each budget. The exit code is 0 only if every page passes.
risks: A page whose content timing never fires is recorded as zero, which passes the speed budget falsely. The browser path is fixed to one machine, so other computers use a different browser and results may not match.
debug: If every page fails, check that the app has been built and the server answers. If the timing is zero, check the page renders visible content. If a browser error appears, check the browser path.
